annotationRationale: Choosing the largest terms gives a universal bound for each number of changes. Arithmetic-series sums determine the threshold, and an explicit selection of 15 signs attains it.
sourceMethod: Follows the official largest-terms argument and first-k odd-number sum, comparing 35² and 36². Explains why selecting the largest terms minimizes the result.

review.mathCheck: The original sum is \(2500\). The largest 14 terms sum to \(1204\), so even the best 14 changes leave \(2500-2(1204)=92>0\). The largest 15 sum to \(1275\), yielding \(-50\). Hence 15 changes are necessary and sufficient, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 5: negate the largest terms, use the first-odd-integers sum, and compare 35 and 36 retained terms. The candidate additionally explains the decrease of twice each changed term.
review.annotationCheck: The extremal choice is correctly assessed, with arithmetic-series summation as support. The strict negativity threshold and an allowed attaining selection are both explicit.
